nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
It is related from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the meaning of
سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ, and he said: "Declaring Allah free of every evil." Abū Jaʿfar said: the explanation of this is that it means putting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, far away from everything the idolaters ascribed to Him of rivals, opposites, partners and children. According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. سبّحت الله تسبيحا ("I declared Allah's transcendence with a declaring"); except that when it stands alone it is definite and accusative without tanwīn (nunation), because at its end there are two added letters and it is definite. Sībawayh reported that some of the Arabs make it indefinite and so make it fully declinable. Abū ʿUbayd reported two other ways of explaining its accusative besides this: that it is accusative as a vocative, i.e. يا سبحان الله; and the other way: that it is not qualified. الَّذِي is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). And he said: سرى and أسرى are two well-known dialectal usages. بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا: ليلا is an adverb (ẓarf). مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ: الحرام is a naʿt (adjective) of المسجد. The root sense of حرام is prevention; so the Sacred Mosque is one in which hunting is prohibited. Abū Isḥāq said: the whole sacred precinct (al-ḥaram) is also called a mosque. إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى: الأقصى is a naʿt of it, and likewise الَّذِي بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ. It is said: the meaning of "We blessed its surroundings" is that the prophets, peace be upon them, who came after Moses ﷺ from the Children of Israel were in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and its surroundings, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, blessed those places by keeping idolatry far from them; and for this reason it was named Bayt al-Maqdis, because it was sanctified (quddisa), i.e. purified, from idolatry. لِنُرِيَهُ is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), which stands in place of أن; its origin is the lām of the genitive.

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: وَآتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ: two objects; and likewise وَجَعَلْناهُ هُدىً لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ. أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا with yāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. ألّا يتّخذوا; the source prints the tāʾ form here.]» is the reading of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, the implied form being لئلا يتخذوا ("so that they should not take"). The reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Kufa is أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا; Abū ʿUbayd claimed that it is on the basis of an omission, i.e. "We said to them: do not take". Abū Jaʿfar said: this needs no omission; «أنّ» «[Translator's note: so printed, with shadda; the discussion concerns أن.]» can have the meaning of أي ("that is"), and «أن» can be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being بأن لا تتخذوا ("that you should not take"). The speech was put in the second person because after it comes ذُرِّيَّةَ مَنْ حَمَلْنا in the second person. ذرية is accusative in four ways: it can be a vocative in construct; it can be a badal (substitute) for وكيل, since وكيل has a plural meaning; it and وكيل can be two objects, as you say: لا تتخذ زيدا صاحبا ("do not take Zayd as a companion"); and the fourth way is with the meaning أعني ("I mean"). The nominative is permissible on the reading of whoever read with yāʾ, as a badal for the wāw; but the badal for the wāw is not permissible on the reading of whoever read with tāʾ: one does not say كلّمتك زيدا nor كلمتني زيدا, because the addressee and the addresser need no clarification.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
وَقَضَيْنا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ: we have mentioned the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that its meaning is "We informed them".
The root sense of قضى in the language is doing a thing in a firm, decisive way; the judge (qāḍī) is the one who makes decisive matters that take effect, and al-qaḍāʾ is the decisive matter that takes effect and cannot be repelled. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū al-ʿĀliya read وَقَضَيْنا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ فِي الْكِتابِ «[Translator's note: the variant reading is not visible in the printed text, which matches the ordinary reading.]», and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir ibn Zayd and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim that they read لَتُفْسِدُنَّ as a verb whose agent is not named (passive). «[Translator's note: i.e. لَتُفْسَدُنَّ; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]» وَلَتَعْلُنَّ, i.e. you will surely become great; the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters and because what precedes it indicates it.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ أُولاهُما بَعَثْنا عَلَيْكُمْ عِباداً لَنا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ: it is said: i.e. We left the way open between you and them. Al-Ḥasan read فجاسوا خلل الديار. Abū Isḥāq said: the root sense of الجوس is seeking a thing exhaustively, i.e. they searched to see whether they could find anyone they had not killed. خِلالَ is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. in the midst of the dwellings.
وَكانَ وَعْداً مَفْعُولًا: وعدا is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and its noun is latent (muḍmar) in it.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ, i.e. We gave you victory over them so that you returned to attack. وَجَعَلْناكُمْ أَكْثَرَ: two objects. نَفِيراً is by way of specification (bayān).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ, i.e. the reward is yours; it is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها, i.e. the punishment accrues to it. That لها means عليها is not said by the skilled grammarians; it is an inversion of meaning, and their citing as proof the ḥadīth «اشترطي الولاء لهم» ("stipulate the clientship for them") is worth nothing. There is disagreement over this ḥadīth: a group related it with this wording from the ḥadīth of Mālik ibn Anas, and it is al-Shāfiʿī's narration from him: «واشترطي الولاء لهم». This is a sound, clear meaning. One says اشترط الشيء when one makes it clear, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 266-
فأشرط فيها نفسه وهو معصم
(Gloss: "So he marked himself out in it [i.e. committed himself to the descent], while clinging fast.")
On the other narration «[Translator's note: the source prints the same wording again here; the other narration is presumably «واشرطي».]» the meaning of «واشترطي الولاء لهم» is "for their sake", as you say: "I honour So-and-so for you". There is another view on it: that it has the sense of a prohibition by way of threat and warning.
فَإِذا جاءَ وَعْدُ الْآخِرَةِ, i.e. the promise of the latter time; the adjective was put in the place of the noun it qualifies. The people of Medina and the people of Basra read لِيَسُوؤُا in the plural; the people of Kufa read ليسوء وجوهكم in the singular, except al-Kisāʾī, who read لنسوء وجوهكم and claimed it was the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. From Ubayy ibn Kaʿb there are two narrations: one is that he read (لنسوءن وجوهكم), the lām with fatḥa — it is the lām of the oath with the light nūn, and the pause on it is with alif to distinguish the light from the heavy nūn; and it is related from him (ليسيء وجوهكم) with two yāʾs and a hamza. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The first reading, in the plural, is indicated by وَلِيَدْخُلُوا الْمَسْجِدَ كَما دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا ما عَلَوْا. On the second reading there are three views: the meaning is "that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may disgrace"; al-Farrāʾ said: "that the punishment may disgrace"; Abū Isḥāq said: "that the promise may disgrace". The lām in both is the lām of purpose (lām kay), and so too in the third reading. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: "and when the promise of the latter time came, We sent them", so this verb is the reply of (إذا), and the lām kay is attached to it. On the meaning of "We sent them" there are two views: one is "We left the way open between you and them and did not make them fear you", so this is figurative: leaving the way open and not instilling fear was made a "sending"; similar to it is أَنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ [Maryam: 83]. The other view: "We sent them against you" means "We commanded them to make war on you when you disobeyed and caused corruption", and this is literal, not figurative. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that for whoever read ليسوآ وجوهكم it is, in his view, the reply without omission, but he implied a verb in «وليتبّروا». Qatāda said: the meaning is "and to destroy that over which they had risen"; someone else said: "and to destroy as long as they remain uppermost". Its true sense in Arabic is "to destroy during the time of their ascendancy", as you say: فلان يؤذيك ما ولي ("So-and-so harms you as long as he holds office").

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the mercy here is the sending of Muḥammad ﷺ. وَإِنْ عُدْتُمْ عُدْنا: it is said: if you return to disobedience, We return to withholding victory. وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيراً: two objects.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: إِنَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ: القرآن is a naʿt (adjective) of هذا, and the khabar (predicate) is in يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ. وَيُبَشِّرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ: أنّ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. بأنّ ("with the news that").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسانُ: the wāw was dropped in continuous recitation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. One should not pause on it, because in the written text (al-sawād) it is without wāw; and if someone paused on it outside the Qurʾan, he could only pause with the wāw, because it is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl), which is dropped only in the jussive or in continuous speech; and there is no alif after it. Likewise يدعو and يرجو: the alif comes only with the wāw of the plural, to distinguish it from the wāw that is the final radical in the singular. Al-Akhfash said: it comes in the plural to distinguish it from the wāw of conjunction. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: it comes to distinguish between the accusative pronoun and the emphasising one.
دُعاءَهُ بِالْخَيْرِ: al-Akhfash said: this is as you say انطلقت انطلاقا, i.e. it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "like his praying". Abū Jaʿfar said: the omission of the kāf is not something that requires an accusative or anything else; there is no disagreement among the grammarians that one says عمرو كالأسد ("ʿAmr is like the lion"), and if you omit the kāf you say عمرو الأسد. The true account of the verse is that the implied form is: man prays for evil with a praying like his praying for good; then the adjective was put in the place of the noun it qualifies, and the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the construct) in the place of the muḍāf.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ آيَتَيْنِ: two objects. Each of them comes in the wake of the other and departs when the other arrives, so they are two signs pointing to One who governs them. فَمَحَوْنا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ, i.e. We did not give it brightness and light like the light of the day; the thing erased is that which is not clearly seen. وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً: it is the sun and its light. لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ: there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "and that you may rest in the night". وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلًا, i.e. We put a separation between one sign and another so that you may take guidance from the proofs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (كل شيء) is accusative by an implied verb, and likewise وَكُلَّ إِنسانٍ أَلْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ. وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ كِتاباً يَلْقاهُ مَنْشُوراً: يلقاه is part of the naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, or if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial). We have mentioned the verse and the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
اقْرَأْ كِتابَكَ: the sign of the jussive and of indeclinability (bināʾ) is the dropping of the ḍamma from the hamza. It is reported from the Arabs: أقر يا هذا ("read, you!"), with the hamza changed; and from this is the saying of Zuhayr: [al-Ṭawīl] 267-
وإلّا يبد بالظّلم يظلم
(Gloss: "…and whoever does not begin with wrongdoing is wronged" — with يبد for يبدأ.)
كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ is in the position of the nominative, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. حَسِيباً is by way of specification (bayān), or if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: outside the Qurʾan حسيبة is permissible.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
مَنِ اهْتَدى is a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَإِنَّما يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ; and likewise وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّما يَضِلُّ عَلَيْها, i.e. his deeds are his own. This is indicated by وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى, on whose meaning there are two views: one is that no one is held to account for another's sin; the other is that the meaning is: no one should follow another and imitate him in evil, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ [al-Zukhruf: 22]. One says وزر يزر, the original being يوزر; the wāw was dropped, according to the Basrans, because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is وزر, وزر and وزرة.
وَما كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا: there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is: We do not punish with the punishment that is a penalty for contravening something that can only be known through being informed, until We send a messenger. The other is that it is the punishment of extermination.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: We have already mentioned وَإِذا أَرَدْنا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها and the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: وَكَمْ is in the position of the accusative, governed by أهلكنا.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعاجِلَةَ, i.e. who does not want reward in the Hereafter, We do not withhold that from him — لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: كُلًّا is accusative by نمدّ. هؤُلاءِ is a badal (substitute) for كلّ. وَهَؤُلاءِ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it, i.e. We provide for the believer and the unbeliever. وَما كانَ عَطاءُ رَبِّكَ مَحْظُوراً: Saʿīd said, from Qatāda: i.e. diminished.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: كَيْفَ is in the position of the accusative, governed by فضّلنا, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), not inflected. وَلَلْآخِرَةُ أَكْبَرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). دَرَجاتٍ is in the position of the accusative by way of specification (bayān), and likewise تَفْضِيلًا. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: whoever of the people of Paradise is high sees his superiority over whoever is below him, and whoever is beneath him does not see that anyone above him is better than he.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: فَتَقْعُدَ is accusative as the reply to the prohibition.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الْكِبَرَ is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿĀṣim; the reading of the people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim is (إمّا يبلغانّ عندك الكبر). The first reading is clearer in Arabic, because أحدهما is singular. The second is permissible, as you say جاءاني أحدهما أو كلاهما ("they came to me, one of them or both of them") as a badal (substitute), because after the verb you have brought in three; the proper form is جاءني أحدهما أو كلاهما. If you wish you may say جاءاني كلاهما أو أحدهما, with كلاهما as tawkīd (emphasis) and أحدهما conjoined.
فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ: there are seven dialectal forms of it. Al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read (ولا تقل لهما أفّ) «[Translator's note: so printed, with ولا for فلا.]» with kasra and tanwīn (nunation); Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa said it with kasra and without tanwīn; the people of Mecca and the people of Syria read it with fatḥa and without tanwīn. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash reported three dialectal forms besides these:
they reported the accusative with tanwīn, the ḍamma with tanwīn, and the ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Akhfash reported the seventh form; he said: one says أفّي, with the yāʾ retained, as if he said "this saying is for you". Abū Jaʿfar said: in the first reading the kasra is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the tanwīn because it is indefinite, to distinguish it from the definite; it is a good reading, and the basic rule when two quiescent letters meet is kasra. Al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that in such words only tanwīn is permissible, and that Dhū al-Rumma made an error in his saying: [al-Ṭawīl] 268-
وقفنا فقلنا إيه عن أمّ سالم ... وما بال تكليم الدّيار البلاقع
(Gloss: "We halted and said: 'Tell on (īh) about Umm Sālim!' — yet what use is speaking to empty, desolate dwellings?")
Al-Aṣmaʿī was fond of rejecting rare dialectal forms that are not frequent in the speech of the eloquent. As for the skilled grammarians, they say: the tanwīn is dropped on the basis that it is definite, and on this basis are the second reading and the third reading — because the fatḥa is light and the doubling heavy — and the tanwīn is as explained above. The ḍamma without tanwīn is by assimilation (itbāʿ), as one says ردّ; and the tanwīn is as we mentioned, except that al-Akhfash said: tanwīn is ugly when you put it in the nominative, because there is no lām with it in the speech — as if he takes its nominative to be as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as one says ويل له ("woe to him"); and he claimed that the accusative with tanwīn is as one says تعسا له ("may he perish").
وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً, i.e. a speech with which you honour them and show them reverence.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ, i.e. from the relative, the orphans, the poor and the wayfarer. ابْتِغاءَ رَحْمَةٍ: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. seeking provision that you are waiting for. فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُوراً: it is said: with gentleness, softness and a promise.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقِكَ: اليد (the hand) is feminine, and العنق (the neck) is treated as masculine and as feminine, masculine being more common, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 269-
في سرطم هاد وعنق عرطل
(Gloss: "…with a long gullet, a forward-reaching [head], and a long neck.")
The ḍamma in عنق was dropped because of its heaviness.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ, i.e. He restricts, and does of that whatever contains what is right. This is indicated by إِنَّهُ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيراً, i.e. He knows what is good for them. On the meaning of «فتقعد ملوما محسورا» there are two views. One is that of al-Farrāʾ: it is in the status of المحسور, i.e. the worn-out, exhausted one; he reported: حسرت الدّابة فهي محسورة وحسير ("I exhausted the riding animal, so it is exhausted"), when you drive it until it breaks down. The other view is that «محسورا» means one who has been overtaken by regret (ḥasra).

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كانَ خِطْأً: خطأ is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, its noun is latent (muḍmar) in it, and the clause is the khabar of inna. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the readings in it.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنى: some of the Arabs lengthen it, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of زانى, because it only happens between two. إِنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً وَساءَ سَبِيلًا: سبيلا is by way of specification (bayān), i.e. its path is evil and its act foul.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ: we have mentioned it. وَمَنْ قُتِلَ مَظْلُوماً فَقَدْ: مظلوما is a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَقَدْ جَعَلْنا: assimilation (idghām) is good, because the dāl is from the tip of the tongue and the jīm from its middle, so they are close to each other; pronouncing it distinctly is permissible. لِوَلِيِّهِ, i.e. the person nearest to him. سُلْطاناً: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: every سلطان in the Qurʾan is a proof. Abū Isḥāq said: whoever read فَلا يُسْرِفْ فِي الْقَتْلِ made it a statement, i.e. the killer of his kinsman is not to go to excess. «[Translator's note: the statement form would be فلا يسرفُ; the source prints the jussive vowelling.]» إِنَّهُ كانَ مَنْصُوراً: there are five views on the pronoun:
it may refer to the next of kin (al-walī), and this is the most fitting in the view of the people of reasoning, because it is the nearest to it. Ibn Kathīr said, from Mujāhid: the slain man was helped; and this is a good view, because the slain man was helped in this world when the killing of his killer was commanded, and in the Hereafter by an abundant reward and the punishment of his killer. It is said: the killing was helped. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning may be "the killing", because it is an act. «[Translator's note: the source names four positions explicitly before the fifth.]» The fifth view is that of Abū ʿUbayd; he said: it may be that the first killer was helped when he killed. This is the most far-fetched and most strained of them.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كانَ مَسْؤُلًا: everything Allah has commanded is included in this, because He has made a covenant with us concerning it.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَلا تَقْفُ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ: included in this is the prohibition of slandering chaste women, of saying about people what one does not know, and of speaking about law and religion on the basis of conjecture, and that no one should say what is not his right. إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُلًا: included in this is the prohibition of listening to what it is not lawful to listen to, and of intending and resolving upon what it is not lawful to look at; know that a person is questioned about all of that. He said أولئك of things other than people, because for everything pointed to that is at a distance you may say أولئك, as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 270-
ذمّ المنازل غير منزلة اللّوى ... والعيش بعد أولئك الأيّام
(Gloss: "Blame all dwellings except the dwelling of al-Liwā, and life after those days.")

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
وَلا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً, i.e. possessing exultation. Yaʿqūb the reader reported مَرَحاً with kasra on the rāʾ «[Translator's note: i.e. مَرِحاً; the source prints the ordinary vowelling.]» as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash said: the kasra on the rāʾ is better, because it is the active participle. Abū Isḥāq said:
the fatḥa on the rāʾ is better, because it contains the sense of emphasis, as one says جاء فلان ركضا ("So-and-so came running"); he made it a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. المرح in the language is insolence and arrogant exultation, and from it come strutting and haughtiness. إِنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الْأَرْضَ, i.e. your strength will never reach this. وَلَنْ تَبْلُغَ الْجِبالَ طُولًا: so one should not be haughty and exalt oneself.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: «[Translator's note: the entry begins mid-discussion, apparently concerning those who read سَيِّئُهُ (rather than سَيِّئَةً) in كُلُّ ذلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ.]» They argued from good things that came before, among them وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً and among them وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلًا كَرِيماً; and Abū Ḥātim argued from His saying «مكروها», not مكروهة. Abū Jaʿfar said: nothing follows from these arguments, because the good things came earlier in the section of commands; then came the prohibition, and after it came كُلُّ ذلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهاً, referring to what was forbidden. And He said مكروها and not مكروهة because it refers back to the wording of كلّ, and it is a second khabar (predicate) of the latent pronoun in كان, and that pronoun is masculine.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) containing the sense of emphasis. عَظِيماً is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: Abū Isḥāq said: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا, i.e. We have indeed made clear. He said: and the meaning of وَما يَزِيدُهُمْ is: the making clear does not increase them إِلَّا نُفُوراً.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«[Translator's note: the entry refers to عُلُوًّا كَبِيراً, a maṣdar of a different form from its verb تعالى.]» I.e. تعاليا, as the poet said: [al-Wāfir] 271-
وليس بأن تتبّعه اتّباعا
(Gloss: "…and it is not by your following him with a following" — with the maṣdar اتّباع of a different form from the verb تتبّع.)

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّماواتُ السَّبْعُ: with the feminine on the basis of the group, and يسبح with the masculine on the basis of the whole. وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ: the scholars have discussed its meaning. Some of them said: it is the glorification that is known; some said: it is particular (restricted); and some said: its glorification is its pointing to Allah's transcendence, Mighty and Majestic, and they interpreted وَلكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ as an address to the unbelievers who do not draw the inference. It is said:
"but you do not understand" is an address to people in general, and since among them are some who do not understand that, [it is said that] they did not understand. إِنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيماً, i.e. forbearing towards those who do not draw the inference. غَفُوراً to whoever of them repents.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
It is said: these were people who, when they heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting in Mecca to call people, would revile him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him that He would put a barrier between them and him so that they would not understand his recitation. Al-Akhfash said:
«مستورا» means ساترا ("concealing"); the passive pattern مفعول may have the meaning of the active فاعل, as one says مشؤوم and ميمون, i.e. شائم and يامن «[Translator's note: printed «ويا من», evidently for «ويامن».]», because the veil is what conceals. Someone else said: the veil is literally "concealed", because it is something hidden from them.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَلَّوْا عَلى أَدْبارِهِمْ نُفُوراً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the basis that it is the plural of نافر; and it may be singular on the basis that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the implied form is: ذو نجوى ("people of secret counsel").

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثالَ, i.e. they said at one time "he is deluded" and at another "he is a sorcerer", to attach falsehood to you. فَضَلُّوا from the path of truth, فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا to it.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: خَلْقاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). جَدِيداً is its naʿt (adjective). جديد has one meaning for masculine and feminine; جديدة for the feminine is a poor dialectal usage according to Sībawayh.

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أَوْ حَدِيداً أَوْ خَلْقاً مِمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ, i.e. imagine whatever you wish; you must die and be resurrected. These verses were among the greatest proofs of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَنْ يُعِيدُنا — so He, Mighty and Majestic, foretold that they would say this, and foretold that they would shake their heads in deeming what He said to them unlikely, and that they would say, along with shaking their heads or after it: مَتى هُوَ. And it was recited to them «[Translator's note: printed «وتلى», for «وتُلي».]», and the matter turned out just so.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: people will come out of their graves saying "Glory be to You, and with Your praise". وَتَظُنُّونَ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا: it is said: they only thought this after the reality which creation cannot escape.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
وَقُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ, i.e. the statement which is best. Al-Māzinī said: the meaning is:
"Say to My servants: 'Say', and they will say." إنّ الشيطان ينزغ بينهم, i.e. he incites the unbelievers against the believers.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ: there is an omission in the speech, indicated by what follows; the implied form is: "Say: call on those whom you claimed to be your gods besides Allah, and let them remove harm from you and shift you from straitness and hardship to ease." This is indicated by فَلا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنْكُمْ وَلا تَحْوِيلًا, i.e. they will not shift you from straitness and hardship to ease and plenty.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: (أُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ) is part of its naʿt (adjective), and the khabar (predicate) is (يَبْتَغُونَ إِلى رَبِّهِمُ الْوَسِيلَةَ). In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah have mercy on him, it is (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ) [Translator's note: the source quotes the reading in the same form as the standard text; the variant itself is not distinguishable here], because before it is (قل ادعوا). The implied sense is: they seek the means of approach to their Lord, looking (to see) (أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ), and so they seek nearness. The difference between these people and those who sought nearness by worshipping the Messiah, peace be upon him, and others, is that these sought nearness while being monotheists, whereas those sought nearness by worshipping other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and so they disbelieved. (أَيُّهُمْ) is nominative by being the mubtadaʾ, and (أَقْرَبُ) is its khabar. It is also permissible for «أيّهم» to be a badal (substitute) for the wāw, with the meaning of «الذي», the implied sense being: the one who is nearest seeks the means, with «هو» suppressed. Sībawayh makes «أيّ» indeclinable (mabnī) on this interpretation. That is a rejected view, and we shall mention what is wrong with it, if Allah wills. Those who are called upon are those who were obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the implied sense is: they call upon them as gods. There is another view on the verse, by which it is connected to His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (ولقد فضّلنا بعض النبيين على بعض): (أولئك الذين يدعون), that is, those prophets who call upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (يَبْتَغُونَ إِلى رَبِّهِمُ الْوَسِيلَةَ). ʿAṭāʾ said: that is, nearness. Abū Isḥāq said: al-wasīla, al-suʾāl and al-ṭilba are one and the same. (وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُ وَيَخافُونَ عَذابَهُ): that is, the obedient ones whom they worship hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, according to the first answer.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (وَإِنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ): that is, the people of a town. (إِلَّا نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوها) by death (أَوْ مُعَذِّبُوها) by extermination, because of their disobedience. (كانَ ذلِكَ فِي الْكِتابِ مَسْطُوراً): that is, in the Book that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wrote for the angels, peace be upon them, in which are the reports of the servants, so that they may infer His power from it.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
(وَما مَنَعَنا أَنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالْآياتِ إِلَّا أَنْ كَذَّبَ بِهَا الْأَوَّلُونَ): the second «أن» is in the position of the nominative, by (the verb) «منع», and the first is in the position of the accusative by it. This is a difficult verse. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, who said: Jarīr narrated to us from al-Aʿmash, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyās, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ to turn al-Ṣafā into gold for them, or to move the mountains away from them so that they could farm. It was said to him: If you wish, you may be patient with them, perhaps We may choose (some) from among them; and if you wish, We will give them what they asked, and if they then disbelieve they will be destroyed as the nations before them were destroyed.
He said: No, rather I will be patient with them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: (وَما مَنَعَنا أَنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالْآياتِ إِلَّا أَنْ كَذَّبَ بِهَا الْأَوَّلُونَ وَآتَيْنا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً). Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied sense in Arabic is: Nothing prevented Us from sending the signs which they proposed except that the former peoples denied their like and so were destroyed and exterminated; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did what held their welfare. If someone says: The former peoples were given the like of this and did not believe, so what is the difference? The answer is that the difference between them is Allah's knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, that among these there are some who will believe, and among these and among their children some who will believe, while those would not believe, nor would anyone who believes be born to them.
(وَآتَيْنا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ): two objects. «ثمود» is not declined as a triptote because it is made a name for the tribe; it may be declined fully by making it a name for the clan. (مُبْصِرَةً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and according to most of the Basran grammarians it is of the relational type (ʿalā al-nasab). Some of them said: «مبصرة» has the meaning of «مبصَّرة», that is, made clear, like «مكرم» and «مكرّم». Al-Farrāʾ said: «مبصرة» means illuminating, like (وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً) [Yūnus: 67, al-Naml: 86 and Ghāfir: 61]. Al-Farrāʾ said: Whoever reads it as (مَبْصَرَة) means something like the saying of ʿAntara [al-Kāmil metre], 272:
والكفر مخبثة لنفس المنعم
(And ingratitude is a cause of corruption for the soul of the benefactor.)
He said: When you put «مفعلة» in the place of «فاعل», it suffices for (expressing) the plural and the feminine. Abū Isḥāq said:
Whoever reads «مبصرة», the meaning is "made clear". (فَظَلَمُوا بِها): the implied sense is: they did wrong by hamstringing it and by disbelieving in its Creator. (وَما نُرْسِلُ بِالْآياتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفاً): it was said that this means the verses that are recited.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: (وَإِذْ قُلْنا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحاطَ بِالنَّاسِ): Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned it. It has also been said: your Lord encompasses people in knowledge, cognisance and management, and that is why He did not give them the signs which they proposed, because of His knowledge of them, Mighty and Majestic. (وَما جَعَلْنَا الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْناكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلنَّاسِ): two objects; that is, a trial by which they were tested, and a charge. The scholars have discussed this vision. Among the best and soundest of what has been said about it is that it is the vision in which he saw (them) with heads shaved and hair shortened. When the Prophet ﷺ was turned back from the House in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya, a group of people were tried by it, so much so that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Prophet ﷺ: Did you not promise us that we would enter the Sacred Mosque? The Prophet ﷺ said to him: Did I tell you (it would be) this year? He said: No. He said: Then you will surely enter it. And they entered it the following year, as the Prophet ﷺ had told them. Among the best of what has been said about it as well is what Sufyān narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (وَما جَعَلْنَا الرُّؤْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْناكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلنَّاسِ): He said: It is a vision of the eye which the Prophet ﷺ saw on the night he was taken on the Night Journey, not a vision in sleep. He said: (وَالشَّجَرَةَ الْمَلْعُونَةَ) is the tree of al-Zaqqūm. Al-Farrāʾ said: (وَالشَّجَرَةُ الْمَلْعُونَةُ) in the nominative is also permissible, making it conjoined (nasaq) to the pronoun latent in «فتنة». He said: just as you say: «جعلتك عاملا وزيدا» and «وزيدٌ». (وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ فَما يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا طُغْياناً كَبِيراً): al-Suddī said: al-ṭughyān is disobedience. Mujāhid said: This is about Abū Jahl.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: (قالَ أَأَسْجُدُ لِمَنْ خَلَقْتَ): the implied form is «لمن خلقته», and the hāʾ was omitted because of the length of the noun (i.e. the relative noun with its ṣila). Abū Isḥāq said: (طِيناً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the meaning is: Shall I prostrate to one whom You brought into being in the state of being clay?

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: (قالَ أَرَأَيْتَكَ): the kāf has no position in i'rab; it is only for emphasising the address. Sībawayh reported: «أريتك زيدا أبو من هو». We have mentioned this, with the disagreement of the grammarians, in Sūrat al-Anʿām. (لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ): ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās that he said: «لأحتنكنّ» means "I will surely gain mastery over". Mujāhid said: "I will surely take possession", like the halter of the she-camel and the riding beast, which is its ḥināk. Someone else said: Iblīs only said this when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said (إِنِّي جاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً قالُوا أَتَجْعَلُ فِيها مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيها وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّماءَ) [al-Baqara: 30].

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: That is, complete. [Translator's note: this glosses (مَوْفُوراً) in the verse.]

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: (وَاسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ مِنْهُمْ بِصَوْتِكَ): this is by way of belittling him and those who follow him and threatening him, because whoever disobeys, his disobedience is only against himself and does not harm anyone else. The Arabs do this by way of threat, and like it is (اعْمَلُوا ما شِئْتُمْ) [Fuṣṣilat: 40]. This only occurs after a prohibition, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited acts of disobedience; just as you say: "Boy, do not speak to so-and-so", then you threaten and warn him, saying: "Speak to him, if you are truthful". Likewise (وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ): it was said that this is by way of a figurative representation; it was said that it is possible he has horsemen and foot soldiers; and it was said that these horsemen and foot soldiers are those who strive in acts of disobedience. Likewise (وَشارِكْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْوالِ وَالْأَوْلادِ): it is that he makes it seem fair to them to spend their wealth and to employ their children in acts of disobedience.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: (إِنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ): it was said that its meaning is "My sincere ones". Among the best of what has been said about it is that he has no authority over anyone, because "the servants" here are all of creation, and al-sulṭān is the proof. Thus said Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: he has no proof over anyone that would require that it be accepted from him. There is a third view: the meaning is that over all My servants you have no power except whispering; and the holder of this view uses it as evidence that none of the jinn can cause anyone of mankind to fall into a seizure. (وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ وَكِيلًا) is by way of clarification (i.e. tamyīz (specification)).

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: (وَإِذا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فِي الْبَحْرِ): that is, the raging of the winds and the fear of drowning. (ضَلَّ مَنْ تَدْعُونَ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ): because you know that they will not avail you anything, except Him, so you turn back and call upon Him. This is among the proofs of the Creator, blessed be His name: that no one falls into hardship, whether believer, idolater or atheist, except that he seeks His help.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: (أَفَأَمِنْتُمْ أَنْ يَخْسِفَ بِكُمْ جانِبَ الْبَرِّ): as a ẓarf (adverbial of place). (أَوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حاصِباً): that is, a stoning from above you.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: (ثُمَّ لا تَجِدُوا لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا بِهِ تَبِيعاً): a follower who would pursue Us in objecting to that or in averting it from you.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: (وَفَضَّلْناهُمْ عَلى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقْنا تَفْضِيلًا): He did not say "over all whom We created" because the angels are superior to them by their obedience and because they have no disobedience. (تَفْضِيلًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the meaning of emphasis.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t:
(يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا كُلَّ أُناسٍ): the implied sense is: Remember the day We call. It is also possible that the implied sense is:
the One who originated you will bring you back (يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا كُلَّ أُناسٍ بِإِمامِهِمْ). We have mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said:
(بإمامهم) means by their prophet; and it is narrated from him: a leader of guidance and a leader of misguidance. Abū Ṣāliḥ and Abū al-ʿĀliya said: (بإمامهم) means by their deeds. Mujāhid said: by their book. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views agree, and people will be called by all of this: they will be called by their prophet, and it will be said: Where are the people of scrupulous piety? And likewise the opposite of this: it will be said: Where is the nation of Pharaoh?
Where are the fornicators? So in this there is rebuke and exposure before all the people for the one who is called by it, or praise and joy for the one called by its opposite. ʿIkrima said from Ibn ʿAbbās: al-fatīl is what is in the slit of the date stone; and its implied sense in Arabic is: they will not be wronged (by) the measure of a fatīl.

nahhas-irab:72-72.t:
(وَمَنْ كانَ فِي هذِهِ): that is, in this world, (أَعْمى فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمى); its implied sense is: blinder than he was in this world. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: This is only permissible — whereas one does not say «فلان أعمى من فلان» — because it is from blindness of the heart; and regarding blindness of the heart one says «فلان أعمى من فلان», while regarding blindness of the eye: «فلان أبين عمىً من فلان», and one does not say «أعمى منه». Abū Jaʿfar said: «أعمى منه» is only not said for blindness of the eye, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because blindness of the eye is a fixed, visible thing, like the hand and the foot; so just as you do not say «ما أيداه», you do not say «ما أعماه». There are two other views on it. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «ما أعماه» is only not said because the root of its verb is «اعمىّ» and «اعمايّ», and one does not form the exclamation (taʿajjub) from what exceeds three (radicals) except with an addition. The second view is that they did this to distinguish (it) from blindness of the heart; and likewise they did not say for colours «ما أسوده», in order to distinguish between it and their saying «ما أسوده» from al-suʾdud (lordship), and they made some of the speech follow the rest. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: They only did not say «ما أقيله» from al-qāʾila (midday nap) because they may say in selling «قلته» (I cancelled it), so they distinguished between the two.
Al-Farrāʾ reported from some grammarians «ما أعماه», «ما أعشاه», «ما أزرقه» and «ما أعوره». He said:
because they say «عمي», «عشي» and «عور». Al-Farrāʾ permitted, in prose and poetry, «ما أبيضه» and (the like for) the rest of the colours, and likewise in his view. [Translator's note: the source's «وكذا عنده» is elliptical here.] Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (وَمَنْ كانَ فِي هذِهِ أَعْمى فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمى) that it may be from your saying «فلان أعمى» (so-and-so is blind), not meaning more intensely blind than someone else. Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is preferable so that the meaning accords with it, because after it comes (وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا), that is, than he was in this world. For this reason it is narrated from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that he said: imāla (inclining the vowel) is permissible in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (وَمَنْ كانَ فِي هذِهِ أَعْمى), but imāla is not permissible in His saying (فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمى). He holds that the alif in the second is medial, because its implied form is «أعمى منه في الدنيا», and if he had not meant this, imāla would have been permissible. Abū Isḥāq said: (وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا): that is, (further from) a path to guidance, because he has come to rest upon his deeds and has no way to repentance.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: (وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ): the pattern of «كاد» is faʿila in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad; Banū Qays say «كُدت», so for them it is faʿultu. It was said that they did this to distinguish it from «كِدت» from al-kayd (scheming).

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: It was said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made him firm through protection from sin (ʿiṣma); and it was said: He made him firm through revelation and by informing him that he should not incline towards them, for they are enemies. One says «ركن يركن» and «ركن يركن», and «ركن يركن» is more eloquent. [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing the two forms (e.g. rakina yarkanu / rakana yarkunu) is not marked in the source.]

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (إِذاً لَأَذَقْناكَ ضِعْفَ الْحَياةِ وَضِعْفَ الْمَماتِ): in this there was the greatest admonition for people, since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed of His ruling regarding the chosen prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, if they were to disobey.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t:
(وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنْها): the scholars interpreted this in two ways:
One of them is that if they had expelled him from the whole land of the Ḥijāz they would have perished; the other interpretation is: if they had expelled him from Mecca. The holders of this view said: They did not expel him; rather, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to emigrate to Medina, and if they had expelled him they would have perished.

nahhas-irab:77-78.t:
(سُنَّةَ مَنْ قَدْ أَرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ مِنْ رُسُلِنا): a maṣdar (verbal noun); that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, established as a practice that whoever expels a prophet perishes — (as) a practice. Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, like the practice.
Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: (وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ) is accusative in the sense of "and prefer the recitation of dawn", and "upon you is the recitation of dawn". Abū Isḥāq said: The implied sense is: and establish the recitation of dawn.

nahhas-irab:80-80.t: (وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ): the maṣdar of «أفعل» is «مُفعَل», and likewise the adverbial of place from «فعل» is «مَفعَل». Whoever said that «مدخل صدق» is Medina and «مخرج صدق» is Mecca has two interpretations: one of them is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him that, so it is an entrance of truth and an exit of truth; and the other interpretation is that the meaning is an entrance of safety and a good outcome, so truth was put in the place of beautiful things because it is beautiful. Whoever said «مدخل صدق» is (into) the Message and «مخرج صدق» is from this world interpreted it by what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised him of His support for the Message, and of taking him out of this world free of major sins. It has also been said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him (to say) this upon entering a town or other (place), or upon leaving it. (وَاجْعَلْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ سُلْطاناً نَصِيراً): that is, a manifest, clear proof by which You help me against my enemies.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: (وَقُلْ جاءَ الْحَقُّ): that is, the command of Allah and His revelation has come. (وَزَهَقَ الْباطِلُ): that is, falsehood, (meaning) disbelief and corruption. (إِنَّ الْباطِلَ كانَ زَهُوقاً): al-zāhiq and al-zahūq in the language mean that which has no permanence.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: (وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ما هُوَ شِفاءٌ): that is, a healing in religion because of the manifest proofs and dazzling arguments in it; so it is a healing for the believers, in that no sickness or doubt afflicts their hearts. Al-Kisāʾī permitted (وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ) as conjoined (nasaq) to «ما», that is: and We send down mercy for the believers. [Translator's note: as printed, the word carries the nominative vowel of the standard text; al-Kisāʾī's conjunction to «ما» implies the accusative.] (وَلا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا خَساراً): that is, they disbelieve and so increase in loss. This is figurative (majāz).

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: (قُلْ لَوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ): nominative by an implied verb, since only a verb may follow «لو», either implied or (expressed), because it resembles the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed of what He knows about them that is hidden from them, saying: if you possessed (خَزائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي), that is, His favour; and mercy from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is favour. (لَأَمْسَكْتُمْ): that is, from spending, (خَشْيَةَ الْإِنْفاقِ); and it was said: al-infāq (here) is poverty; the meaning is: for fear that you would spend and what is in your hands would decrease. (وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ قَتُوراً): al-Kisāʾī reported «قتر يقتر» and «أقتر يقتر»; and Abū ʿUbayd reported «قتر» and «قتور» for multiplicity, as one says «ظلوم» for one who does much wrong.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ): two objects. (بَيِّناتٍ) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «آيات», and it may be in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of «تسع». Al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Kathīr read (فسل بنى إسرائيل) without hamza, which would be by lightening (the hamza), or according to the dialect of those who say «سال يسال». The implied sense is:
Say to the one who doubts: ask the Children of Israel. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned what was said about the nine signs from the Prophet ﷺ and from Ibn ʿAbbās; and what Ibn ʿAbbās said must be based on transmitted instruction (tawqīf), since it is not something said by opinion. The two views are not contradictory, for the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ is to be understood as being about verses that Mūsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought which are recited, except that they are an explanation of these signs. The proof of this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic:
(وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ) [al-Naml: 12] (فِي تِسْعِ آياتٍ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ). (مَسْحُوراً): that is, deceived. (مَثْبُوراً) is from al-thubūr, that is, destruction.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: (قالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أَنْزَلَ هؤُلاءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): because Pharaoh, despite sending for the sorcerers and watching what they did, knew that what Mūsā, peace be upon him, brought could only be from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (بَصائِرَ): that is, proofs that minds perceive. [Translator's note: the source has «حجبا» (veils), most likely a misprint for «حججا» (proofs); translated as the context requires.]

nahhas-irab:105-105.t: (وَبِالْحَقِّ أَنْزَلْناهُ وَبِالْحَقِّ نَزَلَ): because everything in it is truth.

nahhas-irab:106-106.t: (وَقُرْآناً) is accusative by an implied verb. (فَرَقْناهُ): We made it clear; and it was said: We sent it down in separate parts: threat and promise, command and prohibition, and reports of what was and what will be; and it was said: We sent it down in portions. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him, derived something like this, saying: «فرقناه» means We sent down a furqān, that is, a separator between truth and falsehood, and between the believer and the disbeliever. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrima and Qatāda read (وقرآنا فرّقناه) with doubling. [Translator's note: the source prints «وقرآن» here.] It may be that its meaning is like the meaning of «فرقناه», except that it carries the meaning of emphasis, intensification and multiplicity. (لِتَقْرَأَهُ عَلَى النَّاسِ عَلى مُكْثٍ): that is, so that they memorise it and understand it. One says «مُكث», «مَكث», «مِكث» and «مُكُث» [Translator's note: the vowelling of the four forms is not marked in the source; these are the forms usually listed]. Mujāhid said: that is, at a slow, measured pace.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ إِذا يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ يَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقانِ سُجَّداً): that is, in gratitude to Allah and in veneration.

nahhas-irab:108-108.t: (وَيَقُولُونَ سُبْحانَ رَبِّنا): that is, declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, far above promising to send Muḥammad ﷺ and then not sending him.

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: (وَيَخِرُّونَ لِلْأَذْقانِ يَبْكُونَ): it was said: in prayer. (وَيَزِيدُهُمْ خُشُوعاً): two objects.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t:
(قُلِ ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أَوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمنَ أَيًّا ما تَدْعُوا): al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: that is, whichever of the two invocations you make.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view of al-Ḥasan, that is, whether you say "O Allah" or "O Raḥmān". Abū Isḥāq said:
The meaning is: whichever of the names you call upon, (فَلَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى): al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, al-Ghafūr, al-Wadūd.

nahhas-irab:111-111.t: Mujāhid said: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ مِنَ الذُّلِّ): that is, an ally or a helper. (وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيراً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the meaning of emphasis.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t:
Abū Jaʿfar read (وناء بجانبه). Al-Kisāʾī said: They are two dialectal forms. Al-Farrāʾ said: The dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz is «نأى», and the dialect of some of Hawāzin, Banū Kināna and many of the Anṣār is «ناء», O you. Abū Jaʿfar said: The root form is «نأى», then it was transposed (qalb). This is something to be wondered at in the view of the Kufans, because concerning what has two dialectal forms and is not transposed they say: it is transposed, as with «جذب» and «جبذ»; yet in this case, which is transposed, they say nothing of the sort. The proof that it is transposed is that they have agreed on saying:
«نأيت نأيا», and «رأيت رأيا ورؤية ورؤيا»; all of this is from «نأى» and «رأى», and if it were from «ناء» and «راء» they would have said «رئت» and «نئت», like «جئت». (وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ كانَ يَؤُساً): if you lighten the hamza you make it "between-between" (bayna bayna). Al-Kisāʾī reported from the Arabs the omission: «كان يوسا»; and he reported (وإذا المودة) [al-Takwīr:
8], saying: like «الموزة».

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: (قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلى شاكِلَتِهِ): this verse is among the most difficult in the sūra. Among the best of what has been said about it is that the meaning is: Say: each acts according to what is most suited in his view and nearest to being right; and your Lord knows best who is nearest to being right. The Arabs use this after something has been made clear, like (وَإِنَّا أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلى هُدىً أَوْ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) [Sabaʾ: 24], and as a man says to his opponent: "One of us is surely lying"; so the speech has come to carry the meaning of rebuke. That is one view. It was also said: the meaning of (قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلى شاكِلَتِهِ) concerns the times of the obligatory laws only. There is a third view on it, by which the meaning is: Say: each acts according to his own direction and his own way, (فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدى سَبِيلًا); and since He knew, He made clear the truth and the paths.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: (وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي): the scholars have discussed it. It was said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that what was best for them was that He not inform them what the spirit is, because the Jews had said to them: It is in our book that if he explains to you what the spirit is, he is not a prophet, and if he does not explain it, he is a prophet. It was also said: they asked about ʿĪsā, Allah bless him and grant him peace, so He said to them: (الروح من أمر ربّي), that is, something that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded and created, not as the Christians say.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ): an exception not of the same kind as the first (i.e. disjoined); that is, except that Allah has mercy on you and restores that to you. Mercy from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is bounty.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: So the Prophet ﷺ challenged them with that, and they were incapable of it in several respects. One of them is the character of the Qur'an which made them incapable of producing its like: a man among them would hear a sūra or a long verse and then afterwards hear an evening tale or a story, and the difference between the two would be evident. Among the inimitability of its composition is that there is not found in the speech of any created being command and prohibition, admonition and warning, report and rebuke, and other than that, with all of it then being harmonious. Among its inimitability is that it does not change, whereas no created being's speech grows long without changing through contradiction or poor quality. Among its inimitability is ellipsis, concision and brevity, and the indication of a small expression to abundant meaning; and although ellipsis, concision and brevity exist in the speech of the Arabs, in the Qur'an there is of that what is inimitable, such as His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ) [al-Anfāl: 58], that is: if there is a covenant between you and a people and you fear (treachery) from them and wish to dissolve the covenant, then cast their covenant back to them, or say: I have cast your covenant back to you, that is, I have thrown it off, so that you and they are on an equal footing in knowledge; for if you do not do that and you break their covenant, it would be treachery, and Allah does not love the treacherous. The like of this is not found in the speech of the Arabs with the indication of these meanings and the eloquence that is in it. Among the inimitability of the Qur'an is the knowledge it contains of things unseen that had not yet come to pass, since whenever the Prophet ﷺ was asked about anything of the knowledge of the unseen, he answered it; so much so that he was asked in Mecca, and it was said to him: (Tell us of) a man whose brothers took him and sold him, then he became a king after that. The Jews had ordered Quraysh to ask him about him, and they sent that to them from Medina to Mecca, and there was no one in Mecca who had read the scriptures. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed Sūrat Yūsuf, peace be upon him, containing most of what is in the Torah of the story of Yūsuf, peace be upon him. This sign was, for the Prophet ﷺ, on a par with ʿĪsā's, Allah bless him and grant him peace, bringing to life the dead man whom he brought to life by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:90-91.t: (وَقالُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً): this is the reading of the people of Medina. The people of Kufa read (حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ), differently [Translator's note: the source prints both readings identically; the standard reports are that the Medinans read «تُفَجِّرَ» and the Kufans «تَفْجُرَ»], and they all read the one after it (فَتُفَجِّرَ). Abū ʿUbayd said: I know of no difference between them. Abū Jaʿfar said: The difference between them is clear, because the second is followed by «تفجيرا», which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «فجّر», while the first is not followed by «تفجير». Yet what is evident is that the first should be read like the second; this is indicated by the fact that Ibn Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid (حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً): he said: springs; and al-Ḥasan said the same. Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda (حَتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً): he said: springs in this land of ours. This interpretation points to «تفجّر», because «تفجّر» conveys multiplicity.

nahhas-irab:92-92.t:
The people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read (أَوْ تُسْقِطَ السَّماءَ كَما زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنا كِسَفاً).
The people of Kufa and Abū ʿAmr read «كسفا» with the sīn vowelless. Abū Jaʿfar said: «كِسَف» is the plural of «كِسْفة», that is, pieces. «السماء» is mentioned to indicate the plural. The argument of whoever read «كِسْفا» is that it is for a single time. [Translator's note: in the standard reports, Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read «كِسَفاً» here, and the source's attribution of the vowelless reading to the Kufans as a whole is as written.] (أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْمَلائِكَةِ قَبِيلًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:93-93.t: (أَوْ تَرْقى فِي السَّماءِ) is from «رقي يرقى رقيّا» when one ascends; and one says «رقيت الصّبيّ أرقيه رقيا ورقية» (I recited an incantation over the boy).

nahhas-irab:94-94.t: «أن» is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is «من أن يؤمنوا» (from believing). (إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا) is in the position of the nominative, that is, except their saying (أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَراً رَسُولًا). So their arguments were cut off when the proofs became manifest, and they came out with ignorance.

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: (قُلْ لَوْ كانَ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَلائِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); outside the Qur'an «مطمئنّون» would be permissible as a naʿt (adjective) of «الملائكة». The meaning of this — and Allah knows best — is: if there were angels on the earth walking about, not worshipping Allah nor fearing Him. This is the meaning of «المطمئنين», because the worshipper who fears is not at ease. (لَنَزَّلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ مَلَكاً رَسُولًا), so that he would admonish them and call them to what is obligatory on them.

nahhas-irab:96-96.t: (قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be accusative by way of clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).

nahhas-irab:97-97.t: (وَمَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ): the yāʾ was omitted from the script because it was omitted before the alif and lām were added, and the alif and lām change nothing from its state; however, the preferred choice is to keep the yāʾ, because the tanwīn has gone. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: The like of this is only permissible with the yāʾ kept; and the correct thing in his view is not to pause on it, but to join it (with what follows) with the yāʾ, so that one follows both the readers and the experts in Arabic. (عُمْياً وَبُكْماً وَصُمًّا) are ḥāl (circumstantial).
